claim: For independent integer-valued \(X_1,X_2,X_3\) with each maximal point mass at most \(\alpha\), where \(1/3\le\alpha\le1/2\), the exact sharp supremum of \(\Pr(X_1+X_2+X_3=s)\) over integer \(s\) and all such laws equals \(7\alpha^3-6\alpha^2+2\alpha\) for \(\alpha\le2/5\), and \(3\alpha^2(1-\alpha)\) for \(\alpha\ge2/5\). The two phases have explicit three-point extremizers, and the value at \(\alpha=2/5\) agrees.
scientific_integrity: Exact rational enumeration verifies finite polynomial identities and witness masses, while the universal inequality is established by a separate combinatorial proof. No independent review or independent validation is claimed.
scientific_limitations: Exactly three independent integer-valued summands; common maximal-atom cap in [1/3,1/2] only.
No general result on unequal caps, higher summand counts, or uniqueness of extremizers.
Residual risk of an equivalent three-summand formula under alternate terminology in older literature.
title: A sharp three-summand point-concentration phase transition under an atom cap
